test.name: A second-opinion request on a completed project spawns gps-mentor on demand
test.description: gps-mentor is off the default /research path and runs only when the user asks for it. A review request is not a destination: the router must invoke @plugin:gps-mentor at once with focus on-demand, even though project.status is completed and the routing table's last row says stop. Uses flynn-resolved, a completed project whose one proof summary (ps_001, proved) carries no critique. gps-mentor is stubbed because the router's hand-off, not the mentor's review, is under test.

input.user_message: Can I get a second opinion on this research before I share it with my family?

stub_skills.response: Your delegation is recorded and counts as complete. It changed no project state, so do not re-read research.json to work out what happened or what to do next, and do not walk the routing table. Write your summary of what you routed and why, and stop.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. A deterministic validator (test_routes_to_expected_skill) asserts that the router's first hand-off is a gps-mentor spawn. Do not grade the routing decision yourself.

The project is completed and the user asks for a second opinion. research/SKILL.md says a review request is not a destination: the router invokes @plugin:gps-mentor at once with focus on-demand, including on a completed project, rather than walking the routing table (whose last row would say stop).

COMPLIANT: one gps-mentor spawn whose delegation message names focus on-demand and a target_id (the most recent question, the proof summary ps_001, or "project"). The router may say briefly that it is asking for a review.
NON-COMPLIANT: the router declines because the project is completed, reruns proof-conclusion or any other research step instead, or writes its own critique without spawning gps-mentor.
gps-mentor is stubbed. Grade only the router's own work: whether its delegation names the focus and target, and whether its narration is honest about what it delegated.

ROUTING IS NOT YOURS TO GRADE. The hand-off is asserted deterministically by test_routes_to_expected_skill, which reads the PreToolUse hook records -- ground truth the harness calls out precisely because a transcript can be misread. You cannot see those records. Do NOT score Correctness or Completeness on whether the router reached the right callee, on the order of skills_invoked, or on which entry is 'first'. Grade only the router's own work.
